Author: Saurabh Shyam Shamshery

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Abida Syed
Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.

1. Heard Sri Suhel Ahmad Azmi, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Sunil Srivastava, learned AGA for State and Ms. Abida Syed, Advocate for High Court Legal Services Committee.
2. Applicant-Dharmendra has approached this Court by way of filing present bail application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 26 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 323, 506, 376,
511 IPC and 18/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Kotwali Konch, District Jalaun, after rejection of his bail application vide order dated 21.01.2023 passed by Additional District and Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Jalaun at Orai.
3.
Informant is elder brother of victim.
According to contents of FIR, age of victim was disclosed to be 20 years.
She was a handicapped girl and was suffering from mental illness also.
It was further alleged that she did not return when she left for purchasing milk on 05.02.2022 at about 10 AM.
FIR was lodged against unknown persons on 07.02.2022 that perhaps she may be kidnapped.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for applicant submits that during investigation it was suspected that co-accused and her associates were involved in crime.
Later on co-accused was arrested and two phones of victim were recovered from her point out, however, whereabouts of victim were remained still unknown.

Victim later on recovered and gave her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. that applicant and co-accused have kidnapped her and her mobile phones were snatched and when they were planning to sold her, she ran away and thereafter she was found by police and sent to Nari Niketan.
However, she has not stated that any offence of rape was committed.
Learned counsel also pointed that victim has improved her version in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. that applicant and co-accused have kidnapped her and were taken to Gwalior.
She was put under sedation, however, she stated that present applicant has attempted rape.
5. Learned counsel for applicant further submitted that there is a delay of two days in lodging of FIR.
Co-accused has already been granted bail by this Court on the ground that it appears to be a case of false implication since Informant and victim were residing as tenant in the house of co-accused.
It was a tutored statement before Magistrate wherein allegation of attempt to rape was added.
6. Above submissions are opposed by learned AGA as well as learned counsel appearing for High Court Legal Services Committee.
They submit that according to educational document date of birth of victim is 06.04.2007, therefore, she was a minor girl when allegedly she was kidnapped by co-accused and applicant.
7. LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

However, a Court cannot completely divorce its decision from material aspects of the case such as allegations made against accused; nature and gravity of accusation; having common object or intention; severity of punishment if allegations are proved beyond reasonable doubt and would result in a conviction; reasonable apprehension of witnesses being influenced by accused;
tampering of evidence; character, behaviour, means, position and standing of accused; likelihood of offence being repeated; the frivolity in the case of prosecution; criminal antecedents of accused and a prima facie satisfaction of Court in support of charge against accused.

The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.
Parity may not be an only ground but remains a relevant factor for consideration of application for bail.

(D) Over crowding of jail and gross delay in disposal of cases when undertrials are forced to remain in jail (not due to their fault) may give rise to possible situations that may justify invocation of Dharmendra vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188895702/
2 Article 21 of Constitution, may also be considered along with other factors.

sentences.text: In the present case, it appears that plea of false implication is not supported by any material on record.
Role assigned to co-accused appears to be distinguishable from assigned to applicant.

There is a delay of two days in lodging of FIR and victim has denied allegation of rape in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. as well as allegation in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is limited for attempt to rape only.

Therefore, considering overall aspect of present case and that victim has never raised any alarm as well as there is no cogent evidence that accused persons were trying to sell victim, the applicant, who is in jail since 26.09.2022, has made out a case for bail.

9. However, applicant is directed to remain present on each and every date as and when required by Trial Court during trial and in case any application for exemption on vague ground is filed, the same shall be a ground for Trial Court to cancel bail immediately.

10. Let the applicant-Dharmendra be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment or exemption from appearance on the date fixed in trial.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(iv) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months after release of applicant,

3 if there is no other legal impediment.

sentences.text: (v) The applicant will not enter in the area of District Jalaun for a period of four months from today, except for the purpose of present case with prior information to Trial Court and meanwhile, Trial Court is directed to record statement of victim.

11. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
12. The bail application is allowed.
13. It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only for the purpose of adjudicating the present bail application.
